The first zero-valued read observed bounded publication lag; it does not prove those points are permanently absent.
These distributions do not establish universal behavior at every exact histogram edge or extreme finite magnitude.
analysis_notes: Zero-count positive bins participate in fixed-range cursor selection using their full logarithmic indices, even when their numeric endpoints are clipped by raw extrema. They add no percentile mass.
An empty endpoint selected from outside its full bin yields NaN for sum and winsorized mean; a mean with no selected mass is omitted. A reversed sparse-bin cursor remains an ordinary empty range.
A single populated positive bin next to a retained empty endpoint uses that whole positive bin midpoint for trimmed weighting. Selected zero-valued mass contributes to count but not weighted sum.

In that single-positive-bin case winsor tails use whole bins outside the selected bin. A lower tail requires a populated positive bin before it; only then is earlier zero-valued mass included. Outside that case the normal cumulative-rank tail rule remains applicable.

Zero-count positive bins can admit an upper tail without admitting a lower zero-valued tail. Explicit zero and an omitted lower bound differ because zero-valued samples sit below positive logarithmic bins.
